record.paper_title: Aspects of Nonabelian Group Based Cryptography: A Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: Is there a quantum algorithm for the search conjugacy problem in polycyclic groups that lowers the complexity of solving that problem?

evidence.quote: 1. Is there any quantum algorithm for solving the search conjugacy problem for polycyclic group that reduces the complexity of the algorithm?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A group $G$ is called polycyclic if it admits a subnormal series $G = G_0 \trianglerighteq G_1 \trianglerighteq \cdots \trianglerighteq G_n = \{1\}$ in which every quotient $G_i/G_{i+1}$ is cyclic. The search conjugacy problem in $G$ is the following algorithmic task: given as input two elements $u, v \in G$ that are known to be conjugate (i.e., there exists $x \in G$ with $x^{-1} u x = v$), produce an explicit element $x \in G$ such that $x^{-1} u x = v$.

Question: Does there exist a quantum algorithm that solves the search conjugacy problem in (general, infinite) polycyclic groups with strictly lower asymptotic time complexity than the best known classical algorithms for this problem?
artifact.category_tag: quantum algorithms for conjugacy in polycyclic groups
artifact.status_search_result: Recent surveys on group-based cryptography in the quantum era and on polycyclic group-based cryptography continue to discuss quantum resistance of the conjugacy search problem in polycyclic groups as an open question, with no known quantum speedup. The hidden subgroup problem approach for these groups remains poorly understood, and no quantum algorithm achieving lower complexity than classical methods for the search conjugacy problem in polycyclic groups has been reported.

status_evidence.title: Group-based Cryptography in the Quantum Era
status_evidence.snippet: Of particular interest is to show that cryptosystems using infinite polycyclic groups are resistant to cryptanalysis on a quantum computer.
status_evidence.claim: Quantum resistance of polycyclic-group cryptosystems (which rely on the conjugacy search problem) is still being investigated, indicating no known quantum speedup.

status_evidence.title: The Status of Polycyclic Group-Based Cryptography: A Survey and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: The solution of the conjugacy problem is conjectured to be exponential time; cryptosystems based on polycyclic groups are studied for resistance to quantum cryptanalysis.
status_evidence.claim: The status of quantum algorithms for the conjugacy search problem in polycyclic groups remains an open research direction.

status_evidence.title: The Hidden Subgroup Problem and Post-quantum Group-based Cryptography
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses HSP approaches relevant to conjugacy-type problems in nonabelian groups, with no known efficient quantum algorithm for polycyclic groups.
status_evidence.claim: No quantum algorithm is known that lowers the complexity of conjugacy search in polycyclic groups.
